Syllabee

BANANA

Learn to read by syllables: four gentle games with pictures and a friendly voice

Free · Four games · 14 themes · No sign-up

Four gentle games

Four games play over the same words.

  • Syllables

    A word is split into syllables under its picture. The child reads it piece by piece and taps a syllable to hear it. Blur the picture in Settings, and the child taps it to check.

  • Memory

    Picture cards and word cards lie face down. A word card stays silent, so it has to be read; only a matched pair is spoken aloud.

  • Build a Word

    Drag the syllables or letters into place under a picture and watch the word come together. A wrong drop costs nothing.

  • Coloring

    A big letter, number or shape to color with a finger, three pictures beside it, and the letter's sound: "a" as in apple, "b" as in bear.

Fourteen themes of ten words

Split the way phonics teaches: pup-py, ti-ger, ba-na-na. Every picture is drawn for the app.

Coloring

It can be played before a child knows any letters.

  • Letters

    Color a letter and hear its sound.

  • Numbers

    Count the dots on the dice.

  • Shapes

    Nineteen shapes to color and name.

  • MathFree

    Ten pictures colored by numbers: each color carries a sum, read aloud. Numbers up to 10, or 5.

See it played

The themes, syllables that speak, pairs, building a word, coloring letters, numbers and shapes, and the settings for grown-ups: real play on a phone.

Everything else

  • No points, no timers, no stars

    A finished word earns fireworks and a little tune, not a score.

  • Drawn for the app

    Every picture is drawn for the app: 14 themes of ten words, and 30 flags.

  • A friendly voice

    Words are spoken by the phone's text-to-speech engine; an English voice needs to be installed.

  • Settings for grown-ups

    Blur the pictures, choose how many pairs Memory deals, how Build a Word cuts a word, which flags Countries deals and how far Math counts.

  • Nothing to lose

    A wrong drop costs nothing: the piece simply stays where it was put.

  • Phones and tablets

    Upright or on its side; on a tablet held sideways the picture and the word sit side by side.
